Maybe this should be clarified here?

So I tried to do my homework and AFAIU, AES-Keywrap is just some AES-based authenticated encryption (?).

[RFC 3394](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3394):

> Throughout this document, any data being wrapped will be referred to as the key data.  **It makes no difference to the algorithm whether the data being wrapped is a key**; in fact there is often good reason to include other data with the key, to wrap multiple keys together, or to wrap data that isn't strictly a key.  So, the term "key data" is used broadly to mean any data being wrapped, but particularly keys, since this is primarily a key wrap algorithm. 
>
> [...]
>
> The key wrap algorithm includes a strong integrity check on the key data.  If unwrapping produces the expected check value in A[0], then the chance that the key data is corrupt is 2^-64.

See as well "[When do I use NIST AES key wrapping?](https://security.stackexchange.com/questions/40052/when-do-i-use-nist-aes-key-wrapping)]"
